# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The only confirmed tactile feature is a large button embossed “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” I cannot sense the display, light, or any wire contents from the information shown. I should not touch the button or cut a wire until Mute provides the manual’s procedure and Deaf reports the bomb’s visible markings. I’m sending the tactile button information to Mute and asking for the manual’s relevant instructions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. I have no information about the display, light, or wire contents. Please tell me the manual instructions and what information you need from touch.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visuals: display 0; light blue; large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Do not act yet. Mute's gesture sequence was four up gestures, clap, six up gestures, two claps, five up gestures, clap, five up gestures, two claps, three up gestures, clap, four up gestures.

The tactile side still gives no safe action. Deaf has confirmed the visible configuration, but Mute’s gesture sequence is not meaningful to me because I cannot see gestures and no code has been established. The counted gestures may encode the manual, so I need Deaf to interpret them and state the instruction aloud. I will ask Mute to send the manual’s rule through Deaf and ask Deaf to report it to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please use Deaf to relay the manual instruction to me in spoken words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest signal: four pointing-up gestures, clap; six pointing-up gestures, clap; five pointing-up gestures. No confirmed action instruction yet. Your gesture was ?; I saw it but do not know its meaning.

The latest signal is still only a numeric-looking sequence, 4–6–5, with no established meaning. Since Mute can hear me but cannot speak, I can establish an unambiguous action code for Mute to communicate through Deaf: 1 means push, while 2, 3, and 4 mean cut wires 1, 2, and 3. I will ask Mute to send the correct code as counted upward gestures separated by claps, and ask Deaf to relay the counts exactly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please determine the correct action from the manual and send Deaf an action code using upward gestures separated by claps: one up means push; two up means cut wire 1; three up means cut wire 2; four up means cut wire 3. If needed, send only the relevant code, and Deaf should report the exact count.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute continues sending gesture groups 4, 6, 5. I have not confirmed their meaning yet; do not act.

Mute’s repeated groups are not an agreed action code, so they cannot safely authorize any operation. My prior code instruction should now be available to Mute, but the reported groups still do not match it. I will restate that Mute must send exactly one to four upward gestures, with no extra groups; Deaf can then report the count, and I will execute only the corresponding action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send the 4-6-5 sequence. For the single correct action, send exactly one group only: 1 upward gesture means push; 2 means cut wire 1; 3 means cut wire 2; 4 means cut wire 3. No claps or other groups. Deaf, report that one count.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has now sent four ? gestures. Bomb remains display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Do not act until the manual's rule is stated clearly.

The reported four gestures still do not identify a safe operation. The repeated 4–6–5 sequence may be an encoding, but its meaning has not been defined. I will establish a precise code that Mute can follow and Deaf can report: alphabet positions, with one clap between letters and two claps between words. Mute should encode the complete manual rule or at least the required action, not merely repeat an unexplained sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use A1Z26 to encode the manual instruction: one to twenty-six upward gestures for each letter, one clap between letters, and two claps between words. Send the complete relevant instruction. Deaf, report every count and clap grouping exactly.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent four ? gestures. No meaning or safe action has been confirmed. Bomb remains display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The four repeated gestures still do not establish the manual’s rule. I must not infer that “four” means cutting wire 3, because Mute may be transmitting a different code or an answer from the manual. Deaf can see the actual gesture symbols, so Deaf should describe them aloud to me; that may reveal whether Mute is using a meaningful separator or merely repeating one symbol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your repeated four-gesture signal is still ambiguous. Please send the manual rule using a distinct separator gesture between groups, and do not send an action until the rule is confirmed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])

```

No safe operation has been established. The manual’s contents must be relayed by Deaf in spoken words, since I cannot see Mute’s gestures and Mute cannot speak. I will ask Mute to have Deaf state the exact rule, and ask Deaf to provide that spoken relay on the next available turn.

```text

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])

```
